findings.passage: “Two million people that registered to vote, and you have 10 to 15 people, not percent, people, who may possibly have voted illegally in elections,” DuPree said. “That doesn’t even calculate.”
findings.note: Quoted by WDAM (Hattiesburg) on Senate Bill 2588 (SHIELD Act): he questions how common illegal voting by non-citizens is.
subjects: SHIELD Act citizenship check of voter rolls

findings.passage: “When they were born, they didn’t know who they were going to marry. And so, the name that they ended up with in a marriage certificate is different than the name on a birth certificate or different than the name on a government ID,” DuPree said.
findings.note: Quoted by WDAM on name mismatch between a birth certificate and current ID when citizenship documents are asked for.
subjects: SHIELD Act citizenship check of voter rolls

findings.passage: “So, it seems that we’re going down this dark path of putting obstacles in front of people to keep them from voting, do you agree?” Dupree asked of Blount.
findings.note: Quoted in an Associated Press story carried by the Star-Herald, during Senate debate on the SHIELD Act (Blount is the senator he addressed).
subjects: SHIELD Act citizenship check of voter rolls

findings.passage: “We already have problems with people not voting in Mississippi. So, do you think that more people are going to vote if you put more barriers in front of them?” DuPree said. “It’s not logical to think that, if I have a straight line to a door, I’m going to move faster if you put up barriers in front of me.”
findings.note: Quoted by Mississippi Free Press on the SHIELD Act and turnout.
subjects: SHIELD Act citizenship check of voter rolls

findings.passage: “I don’t think it’s legal,” DuPree said. “Hopefully, some judge… will prevent it from going into action and some other learned person or people determine whether it is constitutional.”
findings.note: Quoted by Mississippi Free Press: he hopes the SHIELD Act is challenged in court before it takes effect.
subjects: SHIELD Act citizenship check of voter rolls

findings.passage: “At 1.8 million voters, if 1% is flagged, we’re talking about 18,000 voters that could possibly be thrown off of the voters roll,” DuPree said.
findings.note: Quoted by WDAM on how many voters the SHIELD Act citizenship check could flag.
subjects: SHIELD Act citizenship check of voter rolls

findings.passage: “We can have multiple locations where they can actually fill out the application and get that birth certificate back to them in a timely manner,” DuPree said.
findings.note: Quoted by WDAM: he discusses with the bill's author ways to make birth certificates easier to get for voters asked for proof of citizenship.
subjects: SHIELD Act citizenship check of voter rolls

findings.passage: “Well, like I told everybody else, voter ID is the law,” DuPree told the Jackson Free Press at the Neshoba County Fair in August. “I like to drive 85 miles-per-hour, but you can't in Mississippi, because that's not the law.”
findings.note: Jackson Free Press, while he ran for Secretary of State; the interview was in August 2019 and the article is dated 2019-11-04. The same article states he would keep current photo ID procedures (reporter's words).

findings.passage: “You have a fundamental right to vote, and why do I have to give an excuse to vote?” DuPree said.
findings.note: Quoted by Jackson Free Press on no-excuse early and absentee voting (related to ballot access, not ID).

findings.passage: Increasing access and participation will increase confidence in the process and the outcome of elections.
findings.note: His own answer on the Mississippi Public Broadcasting 2019 candidate page for Secretary of State; general voter access, no mention of ID.
